page: Microsoft Azure E20pds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EPDSv5 series, built on the 64-bit ARM architecture. The host is powered by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz, offering 20 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core and no hyperthreading overhead. It provides 160.0 GB of total RAM, delivering 8.0 GB of memory per core. The server includes 805 GB of local SSD temporary storage without attached discrete GPUs, operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks show solid multi-threaded capability and high memory throughput alongside moderate single-core output. In stress-ng evaluations, the server achieves 1822.88 in single-core and 36030.32 in multi-core tests, placing both within the median distribution. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 1109.0 and a multi-core score of 10649.0. Memory tests display 150.41 GB/sec in large-block uncached read bandwidth and 73.73 GB/sec in large-block write bandwidth. Caching and storage performance is highlighted by 28.38 million Redis SET operations per second, while small-model LLM inference achieves 145.94 tokens per second on 135M parameter text generation.

The hardware configuration exhibits strong resource density, offering an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio and dedicated execution pipelines. Because the architecture relies on single-threaded Neoverse-N1 cores, single-thread compute density is lower than comparable high-frequency x86 alternatives, as observed in single-threaded bzip3 decompression and text processing. However, predictable core performance without resource contention between virtual threads provides consistent multi-threaded stability. The bundled 805 GB local SSD affords rapid local scratch performance without additional disk attachment overhead.

Microsoft Azure E20pds_v5 is well tailored for memory-intensive, highly concurrent workloads. Best-fit use cases include in-memory databases, large Redis distributed cache clusters, medium-scale relational database engines, multi-threaded code compilation tasks, and data processing pipelines requiring substantial memory headroom and low thread-scheduling jitter.
description: Microsoft Azure E20pds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine driven by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. Built with an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, the server features 20 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, 160.0 GB of memory, and 805 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Benchmark testing indicates balanced multi-core capability, yielding a multi-core Geekbench score of 10649.0 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 36030.32, paired with 28.38 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread performance benchmarks register in lower brackets, the dedicated physical cores eliminate noisy-neighbor thread contention across the socket. The integration of high RAM density and high-speed temporary SSD storage positions the instance for memory-heavy, concurrent architectures such as Redis caching clusters, relational database hosts, and multi-threaded data transformation jobs.
